goal: Bare fw detects a live worker via claim-lease heartbeats and, when none is live, spawns and supervises the flywheel-worktree daemon as a subprocess -- showing worker state (supervised/detached/none) in the status bar, prompting detach-or-stop on quit (Enter detaches, s stops gracefully), honoring --no-worker, and adding /worker start|stop.

relevant: .flywheel/specs/00021-FEATURE-unified-cli.md -- FR-2, FR-3, and the worker rows of Error Handling/Edge Cases are this task's surface
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_claims.py -- lease/heartbeat reads for liveness detection (a lease with a stale heartbeat counts as dead, per existing lease-lapse semantics)

packages/flywheel-worktree/src/flywheel_worktree/worker.py -- the daemon loop to spawn, its SIGTERM graceful-shutdown path (in-flight lifecycles finalize to interrupted), and the .flywheel/logs/worker/ log layout
packages/flywheel-cli/src/flywheel_cli/ -- status bar and input bar from the prior tasks
references: .flywheel/specs/00021-FEATURE-unified-cli.md Behavior Specification -- the quit prompt branches and the second-console (detached, no spawn, no ownership) behavior
constraints: Liveness is read from existing task_claims lease state only -- no new store surface, columns, or protocol methods.
Supervision is plain stdlib parent-child subprocess management: no pidfiles, no daemon manager, no restart policy beyond /worker start.
The spawned worker inherits the console's environment and logs to .flywheel/logs/worker/ exactly as a manually started daemon would.

Quit prompt appears only when this console owns a supervised child; detached/external workers never prompt. SIGINT/SIGTERM on the console takes the same detach-by-default path -- never silently kill the child.
Stop means graceful SIGTERM and wait; the in-flight run finalizing to interrupted is the existing worker semantics, not new code.
A second console seeing a live lease shows detached and must not spawn; /worker stop on a non-owned worker shows an inline notice instead of signaling.
Worker death mid-session flips the status bar to dead with a notice; /worker start respawns (the new worker's startup recovery sweep handles stranded lifecycles).
Worker spawn failure leaves the console usable: status-bar error, /worker start retries.

Cover with tests that spawn a real subprocess against a temp store (a trivial child process is fine for ownership/quit-path tests; never a paid agent): no-worker spawn, live-lease no-spawn, detach survives console exit, stop terminates and finalizes, --no-worker.
Run mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on every .py file touched and fix all Pylance errors in the same turn.
Commit with a Conventional Commits feat: message before emitting intent=verify.
non_goals: No management of workers the console did not spawn beyond displaying their state.
No changes to lease/heartbeat semantics themselves.
edge_cases: fw worker run manually while a console supervises its own child: leases keep them off the same task; console state stays supervised for its child.
--no-worker with nothing live: status bar shows none and hints /worker start; queued tasks visibly do not start.
Lease present but heartbeat stale: treated as no live worker; spawn proceeds.
